title: The close-out's ancestor walk treats pending as a verdict and stops one commit short
description:
ciFromAnAncestor (internal/reconcile/closeout_ci.go) walks back for a commit CI ran on. Its loop continues only on CINone:

    if report.State == forge.CINone { continue }
    // A verdict.
    return sha, report, true, nil

So CIPending is taken as 'a verdict' and returned. Pending is not a verdict — it is the ABSENCE of one, and returning it makes the caller hold forever.

Measured on epic/ncv closing Phase 4. The walk from head 0dae1d67:

    0dae1d67 <none>       continue
    f8932575 <none>       continue
    07f8678c <none>       continue
    a454c7fb <none>       continue
    dac27935 <none>       continue
    6e9b201d cancelled x3 -> CIPending -> RETURNED, walk stops
    35f6e9fe success x4   <- one commit further on, never reached

The close-out held on 'CI is pending' while a fully green ancestor sat one commit away, with every change between it and the head under .ticfac/ — exactly the case 9da built this walk for.

The cancelled runs come from 5ob: the run's own checkpoint pushes cancel in-flight CI, and cancelled reads as pending forever on that commit. So 5ob manufactures the pending ancestors, and this defect makes the walk stop at the first one.

Fix: continue past PENDING as well as NONE, and take only a CONCLUSIVE verdict — green or red. That is sound for the same reason the walk is sound at all: onlyRunState proves the ancestor's code IS this tree's code, so a conclusive older verdict describes this tree whatever a newer commit's CI happens to be doing.

Keep the head's own pending answer as the fallback when the walk finds nothing conclusive, so a genuinely-still-running CI still reads as pending rather than as absent.
acceptance_criteria: The walk skips pending ancestors and returns the newest CONCLUSIVE one; a close-out whose head has no CI and whose only conclusive ancestor is green proceeds, with a test built from this exact ancestry
